questions.question: In MySQL, what is the effect of setting autocommit=0 for a session?

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes what happens during a DEADLOCK in MySQL InnoDB?
options: InnoDB automatically detects the deadlock, chooses the transaction with the least undo work as the victim, rolls it back, and allows the other transaction to proceed
Both transactions are rolled back and must be manually restarted by the application
MySQL waits indefinitely until one transaction is manually killed by a DBA
InnoDB prevents deadlocks entirely by using table-level locking in all cases
questions.answer: InnoDB automatically detects the deadlock, chooses the transaction with the least undo work as the victim, rolls it back, and allows the other transaction to proceed

questions.question: In MySQL, what does the DEFAULT keyword do when used in a column definition, and what happens during INSERT if the column is omitted?
